requirements: docs/15 Health and failover / docs/27 §9.2 fallback slots
scenarios: the signed registry names gpt-5 as the approved fallback of gpt-5-mini; the compiled plan carries fallback-1 (LEG_FAILED after initial) before anything runs
the primary answers 503 on every request: its bounded retries are spent and the same run continues on gpt-5 with SlotActivated, a PROVIDER SWITCH and a LEG_FAILED continuation (PROVIDER_FAILED:…)
the fallback reads, edits and completes, verified by the repository's own check; the route reads FALLBACK and the request record keeps the initial leg FAILED
under a registry that names no chain the same outage stops the run with a PROVIDER STAY naming the missing fallback and no continuation

ci.note: every Rust job green on macOS, Linux and Windows; the macOS desktop-E2E job passed on rerun after the known states.spec:268 restart-window race (fix in flight as PR #28)

audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL before: the plan schema had Trigger::LegFailed and the gateway retried a failing provider a bounded number of times, but no binding could declare a fallback, the compiler never emitted a LegFailed slot, and a provider failure always ended the run.
proof: Real Core against a scripted OpenAI-compatible provider whose primary model is down: the approved fallback is prevalidated in the plan, activated through admission on the same run, recorded as a decision, and completes the verified change.
negative_proof: Without an approved fallback the outage stops the run and the STAY is on the log; nothing continues elsewhere.
limitations: The chain is declared on the signed registry entry (the operator's approved profile of the binding); the chain follows the opener, and a stronger continuation slot carries no fallback of its own.
